Timeline::add_months¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::add_months(int months) const

Shift On The Calendar Month Axis¶

add_months() moves each defined instant by a signed number of calendar months. It is the direct expression of rules such as one month after billing date or the corresponding date in the previous quarter. Month lengths are not interchangeable elapsed durations, so this method does not approximate a month as 30 days.

The implementation converts each instant to local calendar fields in tz(), adds months to the year/month pair, clamps the day when necessary, and then resolves the preserved clock fields back to an instant. Hours, minutes, seconds, and all nine fractional digits survive the operation.

Destination-Day Clamping¶

When the original day number does not exist in the destination month, the day is clamped to that month’s final day. January 31 plus one month therefore becomes February 28 or 29; March 31 plus one month becomes April 30. This rule is applied per element because different source dates can land in different destination months.

Example 1. Positive month movement demonstrates ordinary preservation, February clamping, a 30-day destination, and a year boundary in one 2-D call.

const auto calendar = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T08:15:30.123456789Z", "2023-01-31T23:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-31T12:00:00Z", "2024-12-31T23:59:59.999999999Z"},
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    calendar.add_months(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-03-29T08:15:30.123456789+00:00", "2023-02-28T23:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2024-04-30T12:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2025-01-31T23:59:59.999999999+00:00"]
]

Signed Counts And Large Month Steps¶

Positive counts move forward, negative counts move backward, and zero returns the same instants in a new value. Counts larger than twelve are valid: the year and month are normalized together rather than processing one month at a time.

Example 2. A negative month traverses both a leap-year February and a year boundary.

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    calendar.add_months(-1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-29T08:15:30.123456789+00:00", "2022-12-31T23:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2024-02-29T12:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2024-11-30T23:59:59.999999999+00:00"]
]

Example 3. Fifteen months is one normalized calculation, and clamping is based on the final destination month.

const auto source = pluss::timeline::make("2024-11-30T06:00:00Z");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source.add_months(15), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2026-02-28T06:00:00.000000000+00:00"

Local-Time Resolution¶

For a timezone-bearing timeline, month arithmetic preserves the displayed local clock, not a fixed UTC offset. The destination’s timezone rules determine the resulting instant and displayed offset. If the preserved clock fields land inside a daylight-saving gap, the method rejects the operation rather than silently choosing a different wall time. An ambiguous repeated clock is resolved using the first occurrence.

Example 4. The local clock remains 03:30 even when the destination month uses a different UTC offset.

const auto local = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-10T10:30:00Z")
                       .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    local.add_months(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-03-10T03:30:00.000000000-06:00"

Shape, Absence, And Ownership¶

The single count applies elementwise to scalars and every array rank. Shape and timezone metadata are retained. NaT propagates without calendar resolution; empty shapes remain empty. The result owns its output storage and the receiver is unchanged. Logical strides are honored when the receiver borrows a non-contiguous buffer.

Example 5. Defined and absent elements follow separate paths without changing the vector shape.

const auto values = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    {1'704'067'200'123'456'789LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}, "UTC");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    values.add_months(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["2024-02-01T00:00:00.123456789+00:00", "NaT"]

Failure Conditions¶

The normalized destination year must stay in the supported calendar and the resolved instant must fit signed 64-bit epoch nanoseconds. A nonexistent local destination is also invalid. Validation is fail-fast: no partial result is returned.

Example 6. A destination inside the spring clock gap is rejected.

try {
  const auto local = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-10T09:30:00Z")
                         .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
  (void)local.add_months(1);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
